newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta eases vs mark, seen briefly weaker.
newsitem.headline: Peseta eases vs mark, seen briefly weaker.

text.p: The peseta eased against the mark in early trade on Tuesday, in what traders saw as a small correciton after the recent strong rally.
By 0850 GMT, the peseta was trading at 83.61/64 to the mark compared with late Monday's levels of 83.47/48.
"We're seeing a small correction after the gains since Friday which is not surprising. We could go as far as 83.70/83 before turning back and appreciating again," one trader said.
Traders said the correction was sparked after a failure to break the 83.35/40 barrier on Monday. The peseta had made sharp gains since Friday when it soared through the key 84.00 per mark barrier.
A recovery in the mark against the crosses in Europe in early trade after recent losses had given further strength to the correction, trader said.
Traders said the Bank of Spain remained absent from the currency market. The central bank had been intervening for some months to hold the peseta above the 84.00 per mark region until Friday.
Among fundamental influences, traders said they would be keeping an eye on Spain December CPI due on Wednesday and the Bank of Spain's regular repurchase auction on Thursday.
